decisions.reason: Changing the Title font size to 28 pt does not change style names, the PBU prefix, naming language, or naming coverage.
The typography change does not alter the requirement to apply the designated style system consistently across all templates; no candidate attribute requires modification.
The source changes the Title style font size and does not change bullet dimensions, balance, alignment, scaling, or approved appearance.
The Title font-size decision does not change the required behavior, sources, target, or robustness standard for legacy-content migration.
The source does not change Tab-key level transitions, applicable list styles, hierarchy structure, or nested-list alignment.
Changing Title typography does not affect the constraint that pasted content keep the right-hand column within page margins.
The source concerns the Title style and does not change numbered-list alignment or behavior at multi-digit item numbers.
The Title font-size change does not affect users' ability to insert manual line breaks after pasting legacy content.
The source does not change table layout stability, right-column boundaries, or the existing uncertainty about pasted-table adjustment.
The typography value change does not alter the supported Microsoft Word environment or the general operational-reliability requirement.
Changing the Title font size does not change document-content language or default-language configuration.
